breakeven_multiple.definition: Multiple of Oct-2027 NTM EPS (Q3 FY28-Q2 FY29) at which the 2027-10-05 price equals $236.88 (dividends ~0.02% ignored)
breakeven_multiple.read: Consensus-like EPS has to arrive and the multiple has to fall a further ~29% (19.5x to ~13.9x) before today's buyer is flat. That is below AVGO/TSM (~20.6x) and far below any agent's base case, and it happens only if the market starts pricing a decline in FY29 EPS. That is the bear case, weighted 25-28% by agents, not compression on its own.

compression_review.verdict: No. Compression is real and will probably continue, but it should not change a small buy. At 19.5x NTM the panel already assumes 2.5-3.5 more turns of compression and still lands at a fair value of ~$263 with P(close >= spot) ~0.61. A loss needs an EPS break (capex digestion), not more de-rating. The real constraints are position size and overlap with AVGO, GOOGL and VST, plus the low conviction label below, not compression.

sizing.entry: 2 tranches over ~6 weeks: half now, half after the Oct 27-30 hyperscaler capex guides and the ~Nov 17 Q3 FY27 print
sizing.overlap: AVGO (same AI-accelerator and hyperscaler-capex driver; a direct competitor for the same budgets), GOOGL (a top customer whose capex is NVDA revenue and whose TPU competes), VST (AI data-center power, same capex cycle). About $1.46k of ~$2.34k invested already rides AI capex.
sizing.reason: Fact-checks found no thesis problem, and compression is mostly priced in (19.5x NTM at the 10-05 base; 15.09x calendar NTM at the 2026-10-23 close, 14.80x ex-SBC). But the downside scenario (2027-28 capex digestion with an EPS cut to ~12x) hits AVGO, GOOGL and VST at the same time, so ~5% (~$500) caps the AI-capex cluster at about a fifth of the portfolio. Liquidity is unlimited and there are no lock-up or listing issues. Event risk is concentrated in late October and mid-November, hence the staged entry. P(Sharpe beats SPY) is 0.47: an expected ~+11% at the 10-05 spot (now +5.3% to the live 222.19 research target (12m) at the 10-23 close of 210.96: 222.19 / 210.96 - 1, after the close re-mark 2026-11-12 9:26am ET; 213.65 (second gate fix 2026-11-12, +1.3%), 209.11 (Huang-removal card 2026-11-12 01:53Z, -0.9%), the +10.0% to 232.06 (2026-11-10) and the 273.45 and 262.70 quoted earlier were superseded sets) at 38% vol gives a Sharpe of ~0.18-0.2, about the same as SPY's, so there is no clear edge. The 0.47 Sharpe-beat probability and the "low" label are the 10-05 base round's and were not re-scored in this peer-refresh update; sizing itself runs on the combined distribution (allocate.py), not on this text.
sizing.conviction_label_reason: Old scale. The Sharpe-beat probability of 0.47 is essentially no edge. Round-2 checks confirmed the fundamentals but added nothing that raises expected return, the ladder is unchanged from the agents' mean, and the AI-capex overlap with AVGO, GOOGL and VST adds concentration rather than diversification.

Morgan Stanley's $1,224B is our sum of its four Big-4 bars; its $1,641B / $1,760B totals cover eight companies. judgment_calls_for_kilian.question: Export-control tightening on SE Asian intermediaries (Megaspeed, Culper's diversion claim): book a loss of Data Center revenue?
judgment_calls_for_kilian.context: After the CEO probe reports, Congress members asked about chips reaching China via SE Asia (Banks/Warren letter on Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam, Singapore; the Chip Security Act passed committee 2026-03-26). judgment_calls_resolved.question: dc_capture FY28/FY29: keep 0.5701 (set as a band middle), or move to the FY27 anchor or the consensus-implied level?
judgment_calls_resolved.context: dc_capture is NVIDIA Data Center revenue per $ of Big-4 capex. FY27 is built from TSMC supply against capex demand (0.5408 on the companies' basis). FY28 and FY29 book 0.5701, set at the first 11-09 pass as the middle of the FY27 anchor 0.5408 and the then Zacks-implied 0.5995. With the new capex the Zacks-implied level is 0.6409, and a middle between two marks is the method Kilian rejected for hs_capex. Rubin raises NVIDIA content per GW to ~$40B from $25B, but no cited source gives Rubin's all-in capex per GW, so it cannot be turned into capture per $; TPU third-party sales, Trainium outside AWS and OpenAI-Broadcom pull the other way. It is a call because no source nets the two forces.

judgment_calls_resolved.question: Huang removal scenario: book the expected cost of the CEO leaving before the horizon, and at what penalty if he goes?
judgment_calls_resolved.context: Kilian 2026-11-10: size the scenario that Huang is removed and the market penalises leadership weakness, not the fine. Probability: Kalshi on 11-09 had Huang leaving before Jul 1 2027 at ~30% and before Jan 1 2028 at 36% (peak 44% on 11-08) [src 113]; the horizon (~Oct 2027) sits between, so P = 0.34 (our interpolation, derived). Penalty if removed: Larcker & Tayan's 38 CEO-misconduct cases (2000-15) show the termination itself cost -0.8% on average once the scandal was out [src 114], but those are ordinary CEOs; NVDA is founder-led with no named successor. The market's own read: NVDA -12.6% vs SMH over 11-09..11-10 [src 115] while Kalshi exit odds went to ~33%, i.e. about -38% if removed (our calc: -12.6% / ~0.33) (an upper bound, since the move also prices the export/legal tail, e.g. The Information's $7.5B China shipments report [src 110]). Applied as P x penalty on both exit legs. Base $266.57.

options.label: No change
options.reasoning: No cited penalty for NVIDIA specifically; the board and White House back Huang.

options.label: Kalshi 0.34 x typical CEO -0.8%
options.reasoning: Probability from Kalshi; penalty from the only cross-company study of terminations after misconduct; understates a founder with no successor.

options.label: Kalshi 0.34 x market-implied -38% (both derived)
options.reasoning: Probability from Kalshi; penalty from NVDA's own two-day abnormal move over the change in exit odds; NVIDIA-specific but also includes the export/legal tail, so an upper bound.

options.label: P/E x 0.87 (scandal study)
options.reasoning: Cline, Walkling and Yore (2018): in CEO cases ~4% immediately and 12-14% of firm value in total over the following year (abstract); NVDA has already fallen ~12.6% relative in two days.

judgment_calls_resolved.why: It is the only penalty estimate specific to NVIDIA and this event; the cross-company -0.8% is for ordinary CEOs whose exits were expected. Upper bound because it includes the export/legal tail.
judgment_calls_resolved.resolved: Kilian 2026-11-10 card: Scandal study, P/E x 0.87

judgment_calls_resolved.question: Apply the scandal discount to the whole firm value (both legs), or only the P/E leg as booked?
judgment_calls_resolved.context: Kilian picked 'Scandal study, P/E x 0.87' on 2026-11-10. As built, that card's option cut only the P/E leg (weight 0.6), so the research target fell 7.6% (266.57 -> 246.28), not the 12-14% loss of firm value that Cline, Walkling and Yore (2018) measure [src 79]. The FCF-yield leg (weight 0.4) is undiscounted, and that gap is why the leg-weight alternatives now move the target more than 5% (P/E alone 226.33, -8.1%). Applying the same 0.87 to the whole firm value means dividing the FCF yield by 0.87 too.

options.label: P/E leg only (booked)
options.reasoning: What the 11-10 card option did; a 7.6% cut, below the study's 12-14% firm-value loss because the FCF-yield leg is untouched.

options.label: Both legs, x 0.87 on firm value
options.reasoning: The study measures loss of firm value, not of the earnings multiple, so the same 13% applies to both valuation legs; consistent with a moderately conservative base case.

options.label: No scandal discount
options.reasoning: Undo the card; no NVIDIA-specific evidence that the discount persists (WYNN's weekly close was back above its pre-report level by the week of 2018-03-05, about a month after the founder resigned: our own Twelve Data check [src 120]).

judgment_calls_resolved.recommendation: Both legs, x 0.87 on firm value
judgment_calls_resolved.why: The study's 12-14% is a firm-value loss; cutting only one leg books about half of it.

judgment_calls_resolved.question: Leg weights P/E 0.6 / FCF yield 0.4: keep?
judgment_calls_resolved.context: The semis playbook names P/E as the primary method; the set weights P/E 0.6 and the FCF-yield cross-check 0.4. After the P/E-only scandal discount the legs differ by $50, so P/E alone moves the target -8.1%. If the discount is applied to both legs (card above), the legs return to their usual gap.

options.label: Keep 0.6 / 0.4 (booked)
options.reasoning: Weights set at the research round; FCF conversion is a check on NVIDIA's cash-heavy model.

options.label: P/E only
options.reasoning: The semis playbook names P/E as the primary method; dropping the FCF-yield cross-check puts the whole value on the discounted earnings multiple.

judgment_calls_resolved.why: No new evidence on the weights; the gap comes from the one-leg discount.
